title: Keep your king safe
objective: Use your developed pieces to get ready to castle.

commentary_source.name: Uroschess original synthetic lesson
commentary_source.attribution: Original teaching text and simplified Catalan practice line; not a historical game

steps.explanation: Your bishop and knight have moved. The path between your king and rook is clear.
steps.detail: Castling moves the king toward safety and brings the rook closer to the game.
steps.coach_prompt: Your pieces made room for the king. Check if castling is safe.

question.prompt: What move can give your king a safer home now?
hints: The squares between your king and rook are clear.
Castle your king to the right.

tree.feedback: Castling puts the king behind pawns and brings the rook closer to the centre.
Nc3 develops another piece and helps the centre. Your king still needs a safer home in this lesson.

question.other_legal_move_text: That move can be explored. Return and look for a way to improve king safety.

takeaway: Develop pieces first; castle when the king can be safer.
